task.name: mysql tables
task.start: Pointed at this file, in any session the operator chooses (rules kickoff), you build from the files alone: on a checkout of the head of main updated from origin, read them whole before you write anything, and take nothing said earlier in the session, or remembered from other work, as authority. Your label is <model>-<effort> as the root's method model says. Read whole, in this order (root method read): every .rs file and every Cargo.toml under crates/, engines/ and tools/ as merged on main; specs/root.xml; specs/rules.xml; this file; then the files it names. Cut the branch SF-96-mysql-tables-v3-<model>-<effort> from the head of main. Every commit message starts with SF-96 and carries no attribution of any kind; commit, push and open the PR under the GitHub account of whoever runs the build (decision service-accounts). Build what this file says, run its gates, push the branch and open the PR into main titled "SF-96 mysql tables v3 · <model>-<effort>" with the body the root's method pr lists. Show on the screen, as it happens, each step by its number and name, each test run with its result, and each gate. What this file, the root, the rules and the merged code do not say is a stop, not a guess.
task.piece: MySQL's Tables (t02): every option the MySQL engine declares (engines/mysql/src/options.rs) written as rows of its own tables in the namespace engine_mysql (engines/mysql/schema) and read back, so every MySQL sample goes through the cortex's rows and MySQL's and comes back the same. And the kit made to require Tables of an engine that reads. Nothing else: no option added, renamed or removed, no file of engines/mysql/schema changed, no database (t07).
task.before: Merged on main: the registry (t03), the tables interface (t02), the spec check (t01) and everything before them; engines/mysql/owner.toml and engines/mysql/schema as the design session wrote them.
task.after: The store (t07) writes MySQL's rows into the namespace engine_mysql of a schema's database and reads them back.

module.public: nothing: Mysql's impl of Tables, reached by Engine::tables
module.step: card() is engines/mysql/owner.toml; files() is every table file of engines/mysql/schema, each named by its table's full name (engine_mysql.table_options), in name order; rules() is every file of engines/mysql/schema/rules, each named by its rule; seeds() and migrations() are empty. Below, a table is named without its namespace, engine_mysql.

An option's value goes to its column as the variant of the column's type (t02 step 1): a flag as Bool, an integer as Integer, text and a word of one of as Text, exactly as written; a column with no option is Null. A flag whose column is BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false (linear and "columns" of table_partitioning_options, linear of subpartitionings, aggregate of loadable_functions, "desc" of table_key_column_options) is an option MySQL's reader writes only when true (engines/mysql/src/read/table.rs, read/program.rs, read/mod.rs): true is the option true, false the option absent, and read() sets it only on true. A flag whose column is BOOLEAN NOT NULL CHECK true (not_enforced of check_constraint_options, inline of relationship_options) is written as a row only when the option is true. A row is written only when at least one of its columns is not null, or a child row (steps 4 and 6) needs it as its parent; read() sets an option only for a column that is not null, so a row of nulls sets nothing. An option of a part whose typed table (the one steps 3 to 6 name for it) has no column of its name is a row of that part's property table (decision typed-core): database_properties, object_properties, column_properties, key_properties, index_properties, partition_properties or subpartition_properties; one row per option the part has, in the order options.rs declares them, its key the option's key, its value as written (a flag written `true` and only when true, a number in decimal, text exactly as written), its id `<part>.property<n>`; read() sets each back with the value its kind gives.

A namespace's options charset and collation go to database_options by their names ("collation" quoted); encryption and read_only are properties of the database (step 2). A table's options go to table_options, each to the column of its name ("collation" quoted) where table_options has one, and every other to object_properties (step 2), but union and outside_references: union, the list of the tables a MERGE table joins, is one row of merge_tables per entry, in order, its text in table_name, its id `<object>.merge<n>` (its parent row in table_options written for it); outside_references, the list of the foreign keys kept as written, one row of outside_references per entry, in order, its text in text, its id `<object>.outside<n>`.

A view's algorithm, check_option and security go to view_options; its column_list, one row of view_column_names per name, in order, its id `<object>.name<n>` (its parent row written for it). definer, sql_mode, character_set_client, collation_connection, time_zone, follows, precedes and disabled_on_replica, on a view, procedure, function, trigger, event or library, go to program_context. A routine's data_access goes to routine_options and its imports, one row of routine_imports per library, in order, its id `<routine>.import<n>`. A loadable function's soname, aggregate and returns go to loadable_functions; a tablespace's datafile, file_block_size, engine and encryption to tablespaces, its autoextend_size and engine_attribute to object_properties; a spatial reference system's srid, definition, organization and organization_srid to spatial_reference_systems.

A column's options go to column_options by their names ("binary" and "collation" quoted) where it has a column, and every other to column_properties. A key's method, comment and invisible go to table_key_options, its key_block_size and engine_attribute to key_properties; its parts, one shape per column in order, each of length and desc, go to table_key_column_options, one row for each column whose shape holds either, its id the key column's id (t02 step 2), length its length or null, "desc" true when desc is true else false; read() rebuilds parts with one shape per column of the key, JSON null for a column without a row (as MySQL's reader writes it), when the key has at least one row, and sets no parts otherwise. A key holds column parts only: MySQL's reader makes a unique key with an expression part an index, and a primary key holds no expression (engines/mysql/src/read/table.rs, its unique key), so parts and the key's columns are one for one. An index's comment, parser and invisible go to index_options, its key_block_size and engine_attribute to index_properties; an index part's length to index_part_options. A check's not_enforced to check_constraint_options. A link's inline to relationship_options.

A partitioning's linear, algorithm, count and columns go to table_partitioning_options; its subpartition, an object of strategy, by, linear and count, to subpartitionings, by in by_text and linear false when absent. A partition's engine, comment and tablespace go to partition_options, its id the partition's, and its data_directory, index_directory, max_rows and min_rows to partition_properties; its subpartitions, each an object of name and those same options, are one row of subpartitions per entry, in order, id `<partition>.sub<n>`, and that subpartition's engine, comment and tablespace a row of subpartition_options with its id, its other options rows of subpartition_properties.

Every numbered id of steps 3 to 6 is counted from 1 in the model's order, and rows() writes, for every counter id they use (t02 step 2), one row of cortex.id_counters holding the greatest number given under it. An option of any part that steps 3 to 6 do not place is the error of t02 step 5, naming the part and the option; none of the options of options.rs is such an option.
An engine that reads (Engine::read is Some) and has no Tables is the kit's finding `it reads schemas, but has no tables to keep them in`.

tests.how: Rust tests on schemas the MySQL engine reads from SQL text of each test's own, and on the samples under engines/mysql/tests; the rows are inspected as Rows; no test reaches a database or the network.
tests.prove: files() holds every table file of engines/mysql/schema by its full name, and rules() every rule of its rules folder
a flag is written as a boolean, a value exactly as written, and a row of nulls is never written nor sets an option
a flag whose column is not null with default false comes back only when it was true, and is absent when it was absent
an option its part's typed table has no column for is a row of the part's property table, in the order options.rs declares, and comes back the same
a table's options, its merge tables and its outside references are rows of their tables, in order, and come back the same

a view's options and column names, a program's context, a routine's data access and imports, a loadable function, a tablespace and a spatial reference system are rows of their tables and come back the same
a key's parts are rows only for the columns with a length or desc, and come back as one shape per column, null for a column without either
column, index, index part, check and relationship options are rows of their tables and come back the same
a subpartitioned table's partitions and subpartitions, with their options, are rows of their tables and come back the same
every numbered id is counted in a counter row holding the greatest number given
an option no step places is the error naming the part and the option
the MySQL engine passes the conformance kit on every sample, its tables' round trip included, and the kit finds an engine that reads with no tables

task.agent-decides: The names and the decomposition of private code in engines/mysql/src/tables.rs and its tests; the SQL texts of the tests within the items; the granularity of the commits. Nothing else: no option, table, column, id or message other than these.

gates.note: Every gate runs from the repository root. MySQL's live tests (engines/mysql/tests/live.rs) need Docker and are not run here: nothing of this task reaches a server.

gate.expect: every test passes, one per item, none ignored

gate.proves: step 8 on every sample, and that nothing else of the engine changed
gate.expect: every test passes but the ones ignored for Docker, which are as many as on main

gate.proves: the specs and the owners' folders are unchanged and whole
gate.expect: the last line is `spec check: 0 findings`

gate.proves: the repository passes, the kit with tables required among it
gate.expect: the last line is `== All checks passed`

task.owns: engines/mysql/src/tables.rs; engines/mysql/src/lib.rs (the module and Engine::tables); engines/mysql/tests/tables.rs; crates/engine/src/kit.rs (step 8); Cargo.lock.
task.forbid: engines/mysql/owner.toml; engines/mysql/schema/**; engines/mysql/src/options.rs and every other file of engines/mysql/src; schema/**; features/**; crates/model/**; every other file of crates/engine; specs/**; tools/**; docs/**.
task.done: MySQL's Tables on the branch; every gate green and in the PR; nothing outside owns touched. After this task every MySQL sample goes to the cortex's rows and MySQL's and back with nothing lost, and no engine that reads can be registered without tables.
